CHIEF COMPLAINT: Patient presented with acute chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by shortness of breath and diaphoresis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: James Powers is a 66-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with substernal chest pain that began approximately three hours prior to arrival. The pain was described as pressure-like, rated 8/10 in severity, and associated with nausea and lightheadedness. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

HOSPITAL COURSE: The patient was admitted to the cardiac care unit. Initial troponin levels were elevated. Cardiac catheterization revealed a 90% occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. Percutaneous coronary intervention was performed with placement of a drug-eluting stent. The patient tolerated the procedure well and was monitored for 48 hours without complications.

1. Aspirin 81 mg daily
2. Clopidogrel 75 mg daily
3. Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
4. Metoprolol 25 mg twice daily
5. Lisinopril 10 mg daily

FOLLOW-UP: Patient to follow up with Dr. Marc Hart in two weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation referral has been placed.
